memos.headline: S08 and S06 Lead at 52-Week Highs; S05 Breaks Down Into Oversold Territory
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. S08 sits just 0.2% off its 52-week high with +21% over 4 weeks and massive relative strength vs SPY of +20.4% over that period—this is the strongest trend in the group, though RSI at 65 and an 8.7% premium to the 50d mean suggest a pullback could come before the next leg. S06 is literally printing a new 52-week high with RSI 68.2 and the lowest ATR in the universe at 2.14%, making it a low-vol leader I want to own. On the other side, S05 is deeply oversold at RSI 32.5, down 12.3% below its 50d mean and 20.6% off its high, with negative relative strength on every timeframe—this is a broken chart until it reclaims the 50d average around ~365. S07 concerns me: despite a strong 26-week return of +37.3%, the 4-week drawdown of -15.9% and 4.26% ATR signal a volatile correction that may not be done, with RSI at 43 and relative strength vs SPY at -16.6% over 4 weeks.

views.note: Near 52-week high with dominant relative strength (+20.4% vs SPY over 4w); I'd reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~306).
At a fresh 52-week high with low volatility (ATR 2.14%) and strong 12w relative strength of +9.6% vs SPY; would cut on a break below ~335.
Healthy uptrend with +22.6% above 200d mean and only -3.6% drawdown, but flat 4w relative strength (+0.6%) tempers conviction; a close below ~407 (50d area) would change my view.
Strong 4w momentum (+14.1%) but RSI at 72.1 is the most overbought in the universe and the 8.5% drawdown gap to highs suggests resistance overhead; wait for a pullback to the 50d area (~147).
RSI 32.5, -12.3% below 50d mean, negative relative strength on all timeframes—classic breakdown; no interest until a reclaim above ~345.
Down 29.6% from 52-week high and trading 12.5% below the 200d mean; the 4w bounce (+8.2%) looks like a bear-market rally until price clears ~400.
RSI 37.5 with -6.9% below 50d mean and -14.5% 12w relative strength vs SPY; trend is clearly down and I'd need a close above ~249 (50d area) to reconsider.
Longer-term uptrend intact (+21.8% above 200d) but violent 4w selloff of -15.9% with 4.26% ATR makes this untouchable until RSI stabilizes above 50 and price reclaims ~925.
Mid-range RSI 51.1 and flat relative performance leave no edge either way; would get interested on a breakout above ~220 or a flush to ~195.
Flat on every timeframe with RSI 48 and sitting right on the 50d and 200d means—no signal here until it breaks out of the ~142–155 range.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 and S02 Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe. S10 posted 85.2% YoY revenue growth and a 71.5% net margin on $81.6B of revenue with only $8.5B of total debt—an almost unheard-of combination of growth, profitability, and balance-sheet strength. S05's just-filed Q2 is equally striking: $119.8B revenue (+24.2% YoY) with a 93.7% net margin and net income up nearly 4x, though that margin level likely includes a large non-operating gain I'd want to decompose before sizing a position. On the other end, S09 delivered only 2.4% revenue growth with net income collapsing 45.8% YoY to a 4.9% margin, and S02 grew revenue just 2.0% with flat-to-declining earnings and a 5.6% margin on $77.9B of debt—both are textbook earnings-quality deterioration stories I want no part of until margins stabilize. S04 and S03 sit in a comfortable middle: S04 at 38.3% net margin with 18.3% revenue growth is durable, while S03's 76.7% net income jump on 16.6% revenue growth suggests operating leverage kicking in, though $122.6B of debt warrants monitoring.

views.note: 85% revenue growth, 71.5% net margin, and minimal debt ($8.5B) represent the best fundamental profile in the universe; a margin decline below 50% would change my view.
24% revenue growth and $112B net income are compelling, but the 93.7% margin likely includes non-operating items that need decomposition before full conviction.
38.3% net margin on 18.3% revenue growth with manageable $40B debt is a high-quality earnings stream; I'd reassess if margins compress below 30%.
76.7% net income growth is impressive but the 16.7% margin and $122.6B debt load leave limited room for error if revenue growth decelerates.
22% revenue growth and 27% earnings growth are solid, but 14.6% margin and $36.2B debt on only $17.4B revenue make leverage a concern.
Steady 16.6% revenue growth and 26.6% margin are respectable, but $82.7B of debt and decelerating earnings growth relative to peers keep me at neutral.
33.1% margin is healthy but $448.8B of total debt dwarfs the $49.8B revenue base; 10% revenue growth is adequate but not enough to de-lever quickly.
18.5% margin and 7.4% revenue growth are fine but unexciting; $23.9B debt on $21.2B quarterly revenue is manageable but growth is below-universe average.
Net income down 45.8% YoY to a 4.9% margin on anemic 2.4% revenue growth is clear earnings deterioration; I need to see margin recovery above 8% before reconsidering.
Only 2% revenue growth, flat earnings, 5.6% margin, and $77.9B debt signal no durable earnings power; would revisit if margins expand above 8%.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause but Sticky 3.5% CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue Against Duration and Favor Defensives
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly on pause—target upper bound at 3.75%, unchanged over three months after 75 bp of cuts over the past year—while CPI is running at 3.5% YoY, well above target and suggesting the easing cycle is stalled. The 10y yield has surged 38 bp over three months to 4.69%, and the 10y-2y spread has compressed 17 bp to just 0.34 pp, signaling the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates and possibly a late-cycle slowdown. Unemployment at 4.2% is benign (down 10 bp over 3m) but has crept up 10 bp YoY, consistent with a modest cooling rather than outright recession. My regime call is pause/late-cycle with sticky inflation: this favors staples and energy over duration-sensitive growth and banks. A CPI print dropping below 3% or unemployment jumping above 4.5% would shift me toward an easing-resumption call and flip me constructive on growth and banks.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from 10y yields at 4.69% and rising, with no near-term rate relief given sticky 3.5% CPI.
Banks typically benefit from a steeper curve and rate cuts, but the 10y-2y spread has compressed 17 bp and the pause regime limits NIM expansion.
Staples offer defensive positioning in a late-cycle pause with sticky inflation and rising long rates pressuring multiples elsewhere.
Energy benefits from an inflationary backdrop (CPI 3.5% YoY) and is less rate-sensitive, fitting the higher-for-longer regime.
Cyclicals face mixed signals—labor market is stable at 4.2% unemployment but rising long rates and a flattening curve suggest caution.
Without clearer sector mapping, the pause regime and sticky inflation leave me neutral; would need a decisive CPI decline to turn constructive.

memos.headline: S05 Earnings Miss Drives Sharp Negative Tone Shift; S06 and S02 Post-Earnings Sentiment Constructive
memos.body: I am focused today on the divergence in post-earnings sentiment across the universe. S05 reported results on 7/22 and the stock dropped -7.1% into the 7/23 close, signaling a clear negative narrative shift that likely has further room to run given the heavy filing cadence (five 8-Ks since early June including governance changes and material agreements). S06 in contrast saw a +2.5% positive reaction to its 7/14 earnings and continues to generate steady disclosure flow including bylaws amendments and other events through 7/23, suggesting constructive institutional engagement rather than distress. S02 posted a modest +1.2% gain on its 7/16 earnings print, a quiet positive that hasn't attracted crowded bullish coverage yet. S09 stands out for a very dense 7/1 filing covering acquisition completion, delisting notice, and governance overhaul—this kind of event cluster typically generates volatile and confused media tone, and I lack enough price data to gauge whether the narrative has settled.

views.note: Fresh -7.1% earnings reaction with heavy governance filing activity suggests negative sentiment has further to run.
Positive +2.5% earnings reaction on 7/14 and continued active but non-distressed disclosure flow through 7/23 support constructive tone.
Quiet +1.2% post-earnings gain on 7/16 suggests modestly positive tone that hasn't yet attracted crowded attention.
Dense 7/1 filing cluster including delisting notice and acquisition completion creates confused, volatile sentiment that I cannot confidently read.
New debt obligation filed 6/10 and routine other-events filings generate no clear directional tone signal.
Routine governance and other-events filings with no earnings reaction data leave sentiment picture unclear.

memos.headline: Oil Spike and Falling Policy Uncertainty Signal Geopolitical Repricing—Energy Names Favored, Rate-Sensitive Names Watched
memos.body: I note that WTI crude has surged 24.7% over the past month to $93.08/bbl, a move consistent with a supply disruption or escalation in energy-producing regions, even as the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has collapsed 51% month-over-month to 194—suggesting a prior policy shock (tariffs, sanctions) is being resolved or priced through. The VIX at 18.70 and HY OAS at 2.77% are both benign, indicating credit markets are not pricing systemic stress, but the oil spike is a clear outlier that warrants attention for energy-exposed and cost-sensitive names. S06 has filed five 8-Ks in the past two months including one yesterday, which could reflect active corporate repositioning around supply-chain or regulatory developments. I have moderate conviction that the oil move is geopolitically driven rather than demand-driven given the simultaneous drop in policy uncertainty, and I would reassess if WTI reverses below $80 or if new sanctions/export-control announcements emerge.

views.note: Unusually high 8-K filing cadence suggests active corporate maneuvering around policy or supply-chain shifts, but without disclosure detail I cannot take a directional view.
Two 8.01 filings in a month flag potential policy-related disclosures but the macro backdrop of falling uncertainty and stable credit spreads limits downside concern.
If S05 has energy or commodity exposure, the 25% WTI surge is a structural tailwind; the early-June Reg FD disclosure may have previewed positioning for this environment.
Mid-July Reg FD disclosure coincides with the oil spike period; absent detail, the benign VIX and tight HY spreads keep me neutral rather than cautious.
Single 8.01 filing in June with no follow-up; policy uncertainty collapse is broadly supportive but I lack company-specific geopolitical signal.
Reg FD disclosure in June may reflect proactive investor communication around the energy/policy environment; falling uncertainty and stable credit conditions favor names with transparent positioning.
